claim: The female reproductive system is the first to age in the human body with fertility decreasing for women in their mid-thirties and reproductive function ceasing completely at menopause.
source: The female reproductive system is the first to age in the human body with fertility decreasing for women in their mid-thirties and reproductive function ceasing completely at menopause (Broekmans et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Broekmans et al., 2009, which provides external scholarly support for the statement.

claim: In the ovary, aging is associated with a loss in gamete quantity and quality which contributes to infertility, miscarriages, and birth defects.
source: In the ovary, aging is associated with a loss in gamete quantity and quality which contributes to infertility, miscarriages, and birth defects (Reefhuis and Honein, 2004; Mai et al., 2013; Hollier et al., 2000; Ann Johnson et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Reefhuis and Honein, 2004; Mai et al., 2013; Hollier et al., 2000; Ann Johnson et al., 2012) that provide external scholarly support.

claim: The age-dependent loss of the ovarian hormone, estrogen, has adverse general health outcomes.
source: Moreover, the age-dependent loss of the ovarian hormone, estrogen, has adverse general health outcomes (Buyuk et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Buyuk et al., 2010.

claim: Women globally are delaying childbearing.
source: These sequelae are significant as women globally are delaying childbearing and the gap between menopause and lifespan is widening due to medical interventions (Sauer, 2015; Balasch and Gratacós, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sauer, 2015 and Balasch and Gratacós, 2012.

claim: The gap between menopause and lifespan is widening due to medical interventions.
source: These sequelae are significant as women globally are delaying childbearing and the gap between menopause and lifespan is widening due to medical interventions (Sauer, 2015; Balasch and Gratacós, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sauer, 2015 and Balasch and Gratacós, 2012.

claim: Loss of proteostasis and dysfunctional protein quality control pathways are hallmarks of reproductive aging.
source: Although aging is a multifaceted process, loss of proteostasis and dysfunctional protein quality control pathways are hallmarks of reproductive aging (Duncan et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Duncan et al., 2017.

claim: Proteostasis relies on tight inter-regulation of protein synthesis, post-translational modifications, folding, and degradation.
source: Proteostasis relies on tight inter-regulation of protein synthesis, post-translational modifications, folding, and degradation (Basisty et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Basisty et al., 2018.

claim: Most protein lifetimes in mammals fall within the scale from hours to days.
source: While most protein lifetimes in mammals fall within the scale from hours to days (Fornasiero et al., 2018; Fornasiero and Savas, 2023), a subset of intracellular proteins persists for months in rodents (Bomba-Warczak et al., 2021; Savas et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fornasiero et al., 2018 and Fornasiero and Savas, 2023.

claim: A subset of intracellular proteins persists for months in rodents.
source: While most protein lifetimes in mammals fall within the scale from hours to days (Fornasiero et al., 2018; Fornasiero and Savas, 2023), a subset of intracellular proteins persists for months in rodents (Bomba-Warczak et al., 2021; Savas et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bomba-Warczak et al., 2021 and Savas et al., 2012.

claim: Long-lived proteins (LLPs) are enriched in tissues harboring long-lived post-mitotic terminally differentiated cells, such as the brain and heart.
source: These long-lived proteins (LLPs) are enriched in tissues harboring long-lived post-mitotic terminally differentiated cells, such as the brain and heart (Bomba-Warczak et al., 2021; Savas et al., 2012; Toyama et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bomba-Warczak et al., 2021, Savas et al., 2012, and Toyama et al., 2013.

claim: The extended lifespan of LLPs places them at inherent risk for accumulating damage during aging.
source: Although the extended lifespan of LLPs places them at inherent risk for accumulating damage during aging, many of them provide key structural support for the lifelong maintenance of highly stable protein complexes in cells (Bomba-Warczak and Savas, 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bomba-Warczak and Savas, 2022.

claim: Many LLPs provide key structural support for the lifelong maintenance of highly stable protein complexes in cells.
source: Although the extended lifespan of LLPs places them at inherent risk for accumulating damage during aging, many of them provide key structural support for the lifelong maintenance of highly stable protein complexes in cells (Bomba-Warczak and Savas, 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bomba-Warczak and Savas, 2022.

claim: The mammalian ovary is comprised of a fixed and nonrenewable pool of long-lived cells or oocytes.
source: The mammalian ovary is comprised of a fixed and nonrenewable pool of long-lived cells or oocytes.
evidence: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge about mammalian ovarian biology.

claim: In humans, oocytes initiate meiosis during fetal development, and by birth, all oocytes are arrested at prophase of meiosis I.
source: In humans, oocytes initiate meiosis during fetal development, and by birth, all oocytes are arrested at prophase of meiosis I (Hunt and Hassold, 2008; Nagaoka et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hunt and Hassold, 2008 and Nagaoka et al., 2012.

claim: Oocyte cell cycle arrest is maintained until ovulation, which occurs any time between puberty and menopause, and thus can span decades.
source: This cell cycle arrest is maintained until ovulation, which occurs any time between puberty and menopause, and thus can span decades.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about human reproductive biology.

claim: Oocytes are particularly sensitive to protein metabolism alterations because they contribute the bulk cytoplasm to the embryo following fertilization.
source: The oocytes are particularly sensitive to protein metabolism alterations because they contribute the bulk cytoplasm to the embryo following fertilization.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about oocyte biology and embryo development.

claim: Maternal proteins produced during oogenesis are essential to generate high-quality gametes.
source: Thus, maternal proteins produced during oogenesis are essential to generate high-quality gametes (Duncan et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Duncan et al., 2017.

claim: The ovarian microenvironment is a critical determinant of gamete quality.
source: The ovarian microenvironment is a critical determinant of gamete quality and has been shown to become fibro-inflamed and stiff with age (Amargant et al., 2020; Briley et al., 2016; Machlin et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Amargant et al., 2020, Briley et al., 2016, and Machlin et al., 2021.

claim: The ovarian microenvironment has been shown to become fibro-inflamed and stiff with age.
source: The ovarian microenvironment is a critical determinant of gamete quality and has been shown to become fibro-inflamed and stiff with age (Amargant et al., 2020; Briley et al., 2016; Machlin et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Amargant et al., 2020, Briley et al., 2016, and Machlin et al., 2021.

claim: A small number of oocyte-specific proteins have been identified as long-lived, including cohesins and several centromere-specific histones.
source: Although a small number of oocyte-specific proteins have been identified as long-lived, including cohesins and several centromere-specific histones, there has not been a discovery-based approach to define the long-lived proteome of the ovary and oocyte.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge from prior research on oocyte proteins.

claim: The mammalian ovary is a structurally complex, heterogenous, and dynamic organ with follicles at different stages of development, remnants of ovulation (corpora lutea), and a heterogeneous stroma.
source: The mammalian ovary is a structurally complex, heterogenous, and dynamic organ with follicles at different stages of development, remnants of ovulation (corpora lutea), and a heterogeneous stroma (Kinnear et al., 2020; Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kinnear et al., 2020 and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Chase periods of 6 and 10 months represented a biologically relevant reproductive aging continuum as mice within this age range begin to manifest ovarian aging phenotypes, including follicle loss.
source: Using previously established methods (Duncan et al., 2017; Kimler et al., 2018; Perrone et al., 2023; Quan et al., 2020), we determined that chase periods of 6 and 10 months represented a biologically relevant reproductive aging continuum as mice within this age range begin to manifest ovarian aging phenotypes, including follicle loss (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and D), decreased ovulation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F), and increased fibrotic foci in the ovarian stroma (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established methods and by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, D, E, F, G–J.

claim: Mice at 6 and 10 months of age manifest decreased ovulation.
source: Using previously established methods (Duncan et al., 2017; Kimler et al., 2018; Perrone et al., 2023; Quan et al., 2020), we determined that chase periods of 6 and 10 months represented a biologically relevant reproductive aging continuum as mice within this age range begin to manifest ovarian aging phenotypes, including follicle loss (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and D), decreased ovulation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F), and increased fibrotic foci in the ovarian stroma (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: Mice at 6 and 10 months of age manifest increased fibrotic foci in the ovarian stroma.
source: Using previously established methods (Duncan et al., 2017; Kimler et al., 2018; Perrone et al., 2023; Quan et al., 2020), we determined that chase periods of 6 and 10 months represented a biologically relevant reproductive aging continuum as mice within this age range begin to manifest ovarian aging phenotypes, including follicle loss (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and D), decreased ovulation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F), and increased fibrotic foci in the ovarian stroma (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G–J.

claim: MIMS revealed a strikingly higher abundance of 15N containing molecules in primordial and primary stages relative to later stage follicles.
source: Within the ovarian follicles, MIMS revealed a strikingly higher abundance of 15N containing molecules in primordial and primary stages relative to later stage follicles, suggesting that primordial follicles can persist for months with limited macromolecular turnover (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by MIMS data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Primordial follicles can persist for months with limited macromolecular turnover.
source: Within the ovarian follicles, MIMS revealed a strikingly higher abundance of 15N containing molecules in primordial and primary stages relative to later stage follicles, suggesting that primordial follicles can persist for months with limited macromolecular turnover (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is inferred from MIMS data showing high 15N abundance in primordial follicles (Figure 1C).

claim: As follicles progress through the primary, secondary, and antral stages the 15N/14N ratio decreases due to signal dilution associated with the increase of cell number and follicle growth.
source: As follicles progress through the primary, secondary, and antral stages the 15N/14N ratio decreases due to signal dilution associated with the increase of cell number and follicle growth (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Long-lived molecules were significantly higher in granulosa cells within primordial and primary follicles compared to later follicle stages.
source: This change in 15N abundance was most apparent in the granulosa cells where long-lived molecules were significantly higher in those within primordial and primary follicles compared to later follicle stages (Figure 1C and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1C and F.

claim: Long-lived molecules also localized to the basement membrane of some early growing follicles.
source: In addition to granulosa cells, long-lived molecules also localized to the basement membrane of some early growing follicles (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Other somatic compartments of the ovary were additionally found to have higher 15N:14N ratio suggesting enrichment in long-lived components, including steroidogenic cells (theca layer and corpora lutea), stromal cells, and cells within the ovarian surface epithelium (OSE).
source: Beyond the follicle, other somatic compartments of the ovary were additionally found to have higher 15N:14N ratio suggesting enrichment in long-lived components, including steroidogenic cells (theca layer and corpora lutea), stromal cells, and cells within the ovarian surface epithelium (OSE) (Figure 1B and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and D.

claim: The OSE had significantly higher 15N/14N ratio among the mentioned cell types.
source: Our quantitative analysis revealed that the OSE had significantly higher 15N/14N ratio among the mentioned cell types (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 1G.

claim: There is significant enrichment of long-lived, 15N-positive molecules in the nuclei of granulosa cells within primary follicles, and cells within the corpora lutea, the stroma, and the OSE.
source: Lastly, we analyzed the 15N/14N ratios in the nucleus relative to the cytoplasm, which revealed significant enrichment of long-lived, 15N- positive molecules in the nuclei of granulosa cells within primary follicles, and cells within the corpora lutea, the stroma, and the OSE (Figure 1E and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1E and H.

claim: The 15N-positive nuclear signal could correspond to known long-lived nuclear proteins, such as histones, nuclear pore proteins, and lamins, which were previously identified in neuronal, post-mitotic cells.
source: As both proteins and nucleic acids contain nitrogen, the 15N-positive nuclear signal could correspond to known long-lived nuclear proteins, such as histones, nuclear pore proteins, and lamins, which were previously identified in neuronal, post-mitotic cells (Savas et al., 2012; Toyama et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is speculative and supported by citations to Savas et al., 2012 and Toyama et al., 2013.

claim: The 15N-positive nuclear signal may suggest that the DNA itself is long-lived.
source: Alternatively, as these nuclear 15N-hotspots coincided with the 31P signal, which is enriched in DNA and correlates with DNA labeling (Guillermier et al., 2017a), this data may suggest that the DNA itself is long-lived (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is speculative and supported by a citation to Guillermier et al., 2017a and data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Distinct macromolecular components within select ovarian cells and tissue regions persist throughout the healthy reproductive stage, with limited renewal.
source: These results reveal that distinct macromolecular components within select ovarian cells and tissue regions persist throughout the healthy reproductive stage, with limited renewal, and those long-lived molecules persist through the stage where ovaries manifest marked reproductive aging phenotypes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the MIMS data presented in the study.

claim: Long-lived molecules persist through the stage where ovaries manifest marked reproductive aging phenotypes.
source: These results reveal that distinct macromolecular components within select ovarian cells and tissue regions persist throughout the healthy reproductive stage, with limited renewal, and those long-lived molecules persist through the stage where ovaries manifest marked reproductive aging phenotypes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the MIMS data presented in the study.

claim: After 6 months of 14N-chase, 36,222±6768 14N-peptides mapping to 4106 proteins, and 13±5 15N-peptides, which collectively mapped to 33 LLPs across all the biological replicates were identified.
source: After 6 months of 14N-chase, we identified 36,222±6768 14N-peptides mapping to 4106 proteins, and 13±5 15 N-peptides, which collectively mapped to 33 LLPs across all the biological replicates (Figure 2A and B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 2A and B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: At 10 months of chase, 39,637±12005 14N-peptides mapping to 4464 proteins and 13±6 15N-peptides mapping to 15 LLPs were identified.
source: Although the total numbers of both 14N and 15N-peptides and proteins were similar between the two timepoints (39,637±12005 14N-peptides mapping to 4464 proteins and 13±6 15 N-peptides mapping to 15 LLPs), the majority of LLPs identified at 6 months were no longer identified as long-lived at the 10-month chase timepoint.
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS/MS data.

claim: The majority of LLPs identified at 6 months were no longer identified as long-lived at the 10-month chase timepoint.
source: Although the total numbers of both 14N and 15N-peptides and proteins were similar between the two timepoints (39,637±12005 14N-peptides mapping to 4464 proteins and 13±6 15 N-peptides mapping to 15 LLPs), the majority of LLPs identified at 6 months were no longer identified as long-lived at the 10-month chase timepoint.
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS/MS data comparing the two timepoints.

claim: Only tubulins and select histones persisted and were identified as LLPs at the 10-month chase timepoint.
source: Only tubulins and select histones persisted and were identified as LLPs at this aged timepoint.
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS/MS data at the 10-month timepoint.

claim: Gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis of LLPs identified at the 6-month chase timepoint revealed significant overrepresentation for terms related to chromatin, nucleosome, tubulin complex, and mitochondria.
source: Gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis of LLPs identified at the 6-month chase timepoint revealed significant overrepresentation for terms related to chromatin, nucleosome, tubulin complex, and mitochondria (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO analysis data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: LLPs had significant differences in FA between the 6- and 10-month timepoints, with 1.13 ± 0.08% and 1.37 ± 0.12% 15N-remaining, respectively.
source: We found that LLPs had significant differences in FA between the 6- and 10-month timepoints, with 1.13 ± 0.08% and 1.37 ± 0.12% 15N-remaining, respectively (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The discrete pool of proteins that persisted throughout both timepoints showed reduced abundance of 15N at the 10-month chase timepoint, consistent with continual, albeit slow, turnover of the protein pool.
source: The discrete pool of proteins that persisted throughout both timepoints allowed for a unique direct comparison of 15N to 14N-peptide peak intensities. This analysis showed reduced abundance of 15N at the 10-month chase timepoint, consistent with continual, albeit slow, turnover of the protein pool (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: At the 6-month chase timepoint, 15N-peptides mapping to an oocyte-specific protein, zona pellucida-3 protein (ZP3), were identified, indicating that a pool persists without turnover for at least 6 months, but less than 10 months.
source: Interestingly, at the 6-month chase timepoint, we identified 15N-peptides mapping to an oocyte-specific protein, zona pellucida-3 protein (ZP3), indicating that a pool persists without turnover for at least 6 months, but less than 10 months, as long-lived ZP3 was no longer identified at the 10-month timepoint (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Histones and tubulin have been previously identified as LLPs in the mammalian brain and heart tissues.
source: While histones and tubulin have been previously identified as LLPs in the mammalian brain and heart tissues, the 6-month long persistence of ZP3 in mouse ovaries is unexpected and of potential importance to reproductive biology.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge from prior research.

claim: The 6-month long persistence of ZP3 in mouse ovaries is unexpected and of potential importance to reproductive biology.
source: While histones and tubulin have been previously identified as LLPs in the mammalian brain and heart tissues, the 6-month long persistence of ZP3 in mouse ovaries is unexpected and of potential importance to reproductive biology.
evidence: This claim is speculative and based on the unexpected finding of ZP3 as an LLP.

claim: MIMS analysis of ovarian sections captured oocytes at various stages of development, which revealed multiple smaller cytoplasmic 15N-hotspots in addition to the enrichment of 15N-signal within the oocyte nucleus.
source: MIMS analysis of ovarian sections also captured oocytes at various stages of development, which in addition to the enrichment of 15N-signal within the oocyte nucleus revealed multiple smaller cytoplasmic 15N-hotspots (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by MIMS data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In oocytes, a total of 2919 proteins at 6 months and 3234 proteins at 10 months were identified.
source: In oocytes, we identified a total of 2919 proteins at 6 months and 3234 proteins at 10 months (Figure 3B, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 3B and Supplementary file 2.

claim: After 6 months of chase, 146 LLPs were identified in oocytes.
source: Although after 6 months of chase, we identified 146 LLPs in oocytes, only 11 LLPs were identified after 10 months, indicating that by this timepoint a vast majority of LLPs have been degraded and renewed.
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS/MS data.

claim: Only 11 LLPs were identified in oocytes after 10 months, indicating that by this timepoint a vast majority of LLPs have been degraded and renewed.
source: Although after 6 months of chase, we identified 146 LLPs in oocytes, only 11 LLPs were identified after 10 months, indicating that by this timepoint a vast majority of LLPs have been degraded and renewed.
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS/MS data and inference about protein degradation.

claim: GO analysis of LLPs in oocytes identified at 6-month timepoint revealed a significant enrichment of terms related to nucleosomes, myosin complex, and several additional terms related to mitochondria including OxPhos complexes, mitochondrial nucleoid, TCA cycle complexes, and mitochondrial permeability transition pore complex.
source: Interestingly, the GO analysis of LLPs in oocytes identified at 6-month timepoint revealed a significant enrichment of terms related to nucleosomes, myosin complex, and several additional terms related to mitochondria including OxPhos complexes, mitochondrial nucleoid, TCA cycle complexes, and mitochondrial permeability transition pore complex (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO analysis data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: There was no significant difference in FA between the two chase timepoints, with 41±2.9 and 50.8±12.2 15N-remaining at 6 and 10 months, respectively.
source: Overall, there was no significant difference in FA between the two chase timepoints, with 41±2.9 and 50.8±12.2 15N-remaining at 6 and 10 months, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The higher average FA average at 10-month chase is likely due to turnover of proteins with lower FA values at 6 months, which by 10 months would leave the oocyte with the most persistent pool of proteins.
source: The higher average FA average at 10-month chase is likely due to turnover of proteins with lower FA values at 6 months, which by 10 months would leave the oocyte with the most persistent pool of proteins.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the FA data.

claim: The FA values for four LLPs that were identified at both timepoints (Hba, Atp5a, Atp5B, and Hist1h4a) sharply decline between 6 and 10 months, demonstrating protein degradation and replenishment.
source: In agreement, the FA values for four LLPs that were identified at both timepoints (Hba, Atp5a, Atp5B, and Hist1h4a) sharply decline between 6 and 10 months (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), demonstrating protein degradation and replenishment.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: There are no significant differences in total mitochondrial protein abundance at 6- and 10-month post-chase.
source: Our results indicate that while there are no significant differences in total mitochondrial protein abundance at 6- and 10-month post-chase, the pool of long-lived mitochondrial proteins decreased significantly, with the majority of proteins being turned over at the later timepoint.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data on mitochondrial proteins.

claim: The pool of long-lived mitochondrial proteins decreased significantly between 6 and 10 months, with the majority of proteins being turned over at the later timepoint.
source: Our results indicate that while there are no significant differences in total mitochondrial protein abundance at 6- and 10-month post-chase, the pool of long-lived mitochondrial proteins decreased significantly, with the majority of proteins being turned over at the later timepoint.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data on mitochondrial proteins.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of the LLPs identified at the 6-month timepoint revealed mitochondrial proteins and myosins as the two protein groups with the highest FA in the oocyte.
source: Hierarchical clustering of the LLPs identified at the 6-month timepoint revealed mitochondrial proteins and myosins as the two protein groups with the highest FA in the oocyte (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by hierarchical clustering data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Mitochondria exhibited a wide range of FA values ranging from 1.10% to 98.9%, with an average of 55.9±35.1 of 15N-remaining at 6 months.
source: In particular, mitochondria exhibited a wide range of FA values ranging from 1.10% to 98.9%, with an average of 55.9±35.1 of 15N-remaining at 6 months (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Supplementary file 2.

claim: FA values for myosins were markedly higher than both actin and tubulin with an average FA value of 80.97 ± 19.8% for myosins, 31.4 ± 15.6% for actins, and only 8.3 ± 1.4% for tubulins.
source: FA values for myosins were markedly higher than both actin and tubulin with an average FA value of 80.97 ± 19.8% for myosins, 31.4 ± 15.6% for actins, and only 8.3 ± 1.4% for tubulins.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative FA data.

claim: Nearly 81% of the myosin protein pool persists throughout the 6-month timepoint, whereas only 31% of actin protein pool and 8.3% of tubulin protein pool persists throughout the same length of time.
source: This indicates that while all three cytoskeletal components are long-lived, nearly 81% of the myosin protein pool persists throughout the 6-month timepoint, whereas only 31% of actin protein pool and 8.3% of tubulin protein pool persists throughout the same length of time.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the FA data.

claim: Histones were also identified as LLPs in oocytes with average FA values of 7.7±9.8.
source: Histones were also identified as LLPs in oocytes with average FA values of 7.7±9.8.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative FA data.

claim: Mitochondrial proteins, histones, myosins, and tubulins have been previously identified as LLPs in brain and heart tissues, which are known to contain long-lived terminally differentiated cells.
source: Mitochondrial proteins, histones, myosins, and tubulins have been previously identified as LLPs in brain and heart tissues, which are known to contain long-lived terminally differentiated cells (i.e. neurons in the brain and cardiac myocytes in the heart) (Bomba-Warczak et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bomba-Warczak et al., 2021.

claim: This is the first time that a subset of the same proteins has been identified as long-lived in the germ cell.
source: Importantly, however, this is the first time that a subset of the same proteins has been identified as long-lived in the germ cell (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is based on the novelty of the findings in this study.

claim: The FA of mitochondrial LLPs in the brain (10.2 ± 6.6%) and myosins in the heart (4.6 ± 8.1%) is much lower than in the same LLPs quantified in the oocyte (55.9±35.1).
source: Interestingly, the FA of mitochondrial LLPs in the brain (10.2 ± 6.6%) (Bomba-Warczak et al., 2021) and myosins in the heart (4.6 ± 8.1%) (Bomba-Warczak et al., 2021) is much lower than in the same LLPs quantified in the oocyte (55.9±35.1) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative data shown in Figure 3D and citation to Bomba-Warczak et al., 2021.

claim: Histones were less long-lived in the oocyte compared to the brain.
source: In contrast, histones were less long-lived in the oocyte compared to the brain, and there was no significant difference observed for tubulins (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: There was no significant difference observed for tubulins between oocyte and brain.
source: In contrast, histones were less long-lived in the oocyte compared to the brain, and there was no significant difference observed for tubulins (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Although the identity of LLPs may be conserved across tissues with long-lived cells, differences in FA may reflect tissue-specific functions and requirements.
source: Thus, although the identity of LLPs may be conserved across tissues with long-lived cells, differences in FA may reflect tissue-specific functions and requirements.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparative data across tissues.

claim: Long-lived macromolecules localized throughout the ovary including the follicular compartment with prominent signals in the granulosa cells of primordial and primary follicles relative to later stage growing follicles.
source: Our findings provide a novel framework for how long-lived structures may regulate gamete quality. Long-lived macromolecules localized throughout the ovary including the follicular compartment with prominent signals in the granulosa cells of primordial and primary follicles relative to later stage growing follicles.
evidence: This claim is based on the MIMS data presented in the study.

claim: The squamous pre-granulosa cells surrounding the oocyte within primordial follicles form early in development which coincided with the 15N-labeling pulse period.
source: These findings are consistent with the knowledge that the squamous pre-granulosa cells surrounding the oocyte within primordial follicles form early in development which coincided with the 15N-labeling pulse period.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about follicle development.

source: These squamous granulosa cells are generally thought to lack the ability to undergo mitotic division until follicles are activated to grow, so it is not surprising that we observed long-lived macromolecules persisting within them (Oktay et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Oktay et al., 1997.

claim: Granulosa cells in growing follicles are generated by cell divisions that take place during follicle activation and growth which coincided with the 14N-chase period.
source: In contrast, granulosa cells in growing follicles are generated by cell divisions that take place during follicle activation and growth which coincided with the 14N-chase period.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about follicle development and the experimental design.

claim: Long-lived structures (i.e. enriched with 15N) were diluted through cell divisions during follicle growth.
source: Thus, long-lived structures (i.e. enriched with 15N) were diluted through cell divisions during follicle growth.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental design and data.

claim: During follicle growth, granulosa cells proliferate and differentiate adding new pools of synthesized proteins and molecules.
source: Moreover, during follicle growth, granulosa cells proliferate and differentiate adding new pools of synthesized proteins and molecules.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about follicle development.

claim: Macromolecules formed early in development can persist in squamous granulosa cells for months.
source: Our results demonstrate that macromolecules formed early in development can persist in squamous granulosa cells for months.
evidence: This claim is based on the MIMS data presented in the study.

claim: It is possible that long-lived molecules will accumulate more damage in primordial follicles that remain quiescent for longer periods relative to those that activate earlier.
source: Thus, it is possible that these long-lived molecules will accumulate more damage in primordial follicles that remain quiescent for longer periods relative to those that activate earlier.
evidence: This claim is speculative and based on inference from the data.

claim: The OSE is highly dynamic due to repeated post-ovulation wound healing and repair.
source: The OSE is highly dynamic due to repeated post-ovulation wound healing and repair, and its regenerative capacity occurs through a somatic stem/progenitor cell-mediated process (Szotek et al., 2008).
